# Refactor: decompose `src/commands/interview.ts` god class

**File:** `src/commands/interview.ts` — 1,630 lines, 41 exports, 9 logical sections.

## Problem statement

`src/commands/interview.ts` carries the whole `wl interview` backend — clarifying-section
detection, Q/A parsing and lossless re-serialisation, the producer-review explanation
(LLM + structured fallback), LLM-assisted question extraction, the interactive walkthrough
loop, readline plumbing and Commander registration — in one 1,630-line module. It breaches
the 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted for WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7, so navigating,
reviewing and safely changing any one concern means holding the whole file in view.

## Users

- **Agents implementing interview/LLM changes** — need one concern (e.g. the answer
  re-serialiser, or the extraction prompt) locatable by file search instead of by reading
  1,630 lines; a monolith inflates context cost and increases the chance of editing the
  wrong helper with a similar name (`cleanQuestion` vs `firstLine` vs `truncateBytes`).
- **Reviewers/auditors** — need a diff whose blast radius is legible from the touched
  module boundary.
- **Producers running `wl interview`** — benefit indirectly: behaviour-preserving
  decomposition lowers the regression risk of every future change to the command.

Example user stories:

- As an agent fixing a Q/A parsing defect, I want the parser and re-serialiser in one
  focused module, so that I can reason about round-trip losslessness without loading the
  LLM and Commander code.
- As a reviewer, I want each extracted module to state one responsibility, so that I can
  judge a diff against a single boundary.
- As a maintainer, I want the `wl interview` command behaviour and the public module
  surface unchanged, so that no test, registry entry or documented flag needs reworking.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Ceiling met.** `src/commands/interview.ts` and every file under `src/interview/` is
   ≤ 1,000 lines (target: largest extracted module ≤ 500). Evidence recorded in the work
   item as `wc -l` output for the module family.
2. **Public surface unchanged.** All 41 current exports of `src/commands/interview.ts`
   (2 section, 4 Q/A, 15 explanation, 11 extraction, 5 loop, 4 registration) plus the
   default `register` export remain importable from the unchanged specifier
   `src/commands/interview.js` with identical names, kinds and signatures; the barrel
   re-exports the full surface. `src/command-registry.ts`
   (`interview: () => import('./commands/interview.js')`) is untouched and needs no edit.
3. **Move-only, behaviour-preserving.** No logic, regex, message, ordering or flag
   changes. Test assertions, fixtures, `describe` titles and mock targets are unmodified;
   the only mechanical test change permitted is the lockstep split of the oversized suite
   `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` (1,696 lines): every resulting file is ≤ 1,000 lines,
   `describe` groups move verbatim and only import paths change. Test count is preserved
   (the split neither adds nor drops a test).
4. **No circular imports, one direction only.** Extracted modules import concrete siblings
   and `../lib/*`, `../config.js`, `../types.js`; **no** `src/interview/*` module imports
   the `src/commands/interview.ts` barrel. The dependency direction is
   `commands/interview.ts` → `interview/*`.
5. **Responsibilities documented.** Every new module carries a one-line module doc comment
   naming its single responsibility, and existing provenance comments/work-item ids
   (`WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67`, `WL-0MUUAMP7M008Z4GK`, `WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF`,
   `WL-0MUX2W8IN005RW66`, `WL-0MUQ0VP800068DNX`) move with their code.
6. **Builds and tests.** `npm run build` (tsc, NodeNext, `rootDir: src`) is green and the
   full project test suite passes via `/skill:test`.
7. **Documentation updated.** All related documentation reflects the changes, including
   code comments, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (command/module map), `CLI.md` if any wording
   drifts, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries. `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded
   (release pipeline).

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate code and update imports only. No "while we're here" rewrites, no
  renames of public symbols, no regex or prompt-text edits. Any incidental improvement
  found en route becomes a separate `discovered-from` work item.
- **Layout: mirror `src/doctor/`.** Helpers for a single command live in a top-level
  feature directory (`src/doctor/*` ← `src/commands/doctor.ts`); this item follows that
  established precedent with `src/interview/*`. The entry file stays
  `src/commands/interview.ts` so the ESM specifier `./commands/interview.js` keeps
  resolving to `dist/commands/interview.js` under NodeNext (a directory-index barrel
  `interview/index.ts` would break that specifier).
- **No new dependencies.** Only existing imports (`../lib/llm.js`,
  `../lib/progress-feedback.js`, `../config.js`, `../mutation-lock.js`, `../types.js`,
  `../cli-types.js`, `readline`) may be used by the extracted modules.
- **No behaviour-parity tooling in scope.** A repo-wide 1,000-line guard is a separate
  open item (WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL, `discovered-from` the sweep); this item verifies the
  ceiling with `wc -l` evidence plus a small structural assertion (see Risks).
- **Escaped backticks** only in written content; Markdown otherwise.

## Existing state

`src/commands/interview.ts` — 1,630 lines, 41 exports, single default `register`, no
module-level mutable state (only `const` regexes/constants). Section map (current `dev`):

| Lines | Section | Exports |
|---|---|---|
| 1–70 | File doc comment + imports | — |
| 71–116 | Section markers (regexes, `INSERT_WRAPPER`) | — (all private) |
| 117–160 | Section extraction | `ClarifyingSection`, `extractClarifyingSection` |
| 161–564 | Q/A parsing and re-serialisation | `ClarifyingQAPair`, `parseQAPairs`, `rebuildQAPairs`, `rebuildDescription` |
| 565–873 | Producer-review explanation | 15 (caps, context/deps types, prompt, render, fallback, LLM result) |
| 874–1052 | LLM-assisted question extraction | 11 (instruction, caps, prompt, parser, result, extract fns, section insert/merge) |
| 1053–1260 | Core interview loop | `InterviewStore`, `InterviewIO`, `InterviewOutcome`, `InterviewRunOptions`, `runInterview` |
| 1261–1291 | Interactive input | — (`createPromptLoop` private) |
| 1292–1630 | Types + command registration | `InterviewPromptLoop`, `InterviewCommandDeps`, `defaultClearPrompt`, `register` (default) |

Consumers: exactly one production importer — `src/command-registry.ts` (dynamic import,
default export only) — and one test file, `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` (1,696 lines, 19
top-level `describe` blocks, no `vi.mock`, imports 11 named exports + default). No file in
`src/`, `packages/`, `scripts/` or `bench/` imports any other symbol from the module, and
no documentation references the file path.

## Desired change

Extract cohesive modules under `src/interview/`, leaving `src/commands/interview.ts` as the
command entry (registration + interactive plumbing) **and** the public barrel. Proposed map
(export attribution is exhaustive — every current export belongs to exactly one row):

| Module | Responsibility | Exports moved | Est. lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/commands/interview.ts` (entry + barrel) | Commander registration, `register` action flow, prompt loop, deps surface, re-export of the full public surface | `InterviewPromptLoop`, `InterviewCommandDeps`, `defaultClearPrompt`, `register` (default) + all re-exports | ~400 |
| `src/interview/section.ts` | Clarifying-section heading detection and extraction | `ClarifyingSection`, `extractClarifyingSection` | ~95 |
| `src/interview/qa.ts` | Q/A parsing, answer-region computation and lossless re-serialisation | `ClarifyingQAPair`, `parseQAPairs`, `rebuildQAPairs`, `rebuildDescription` | ~400 |
| `src/interview/explanation.ts` | Producer-review explanation: evidence formatting, prompt, render, structured fallback, LLM call | 15 exports | ~310 |
| `src/interview/extraction.ts` | LLM-assisted question extraction plus canonical-section insert/merge | 11 exports | ~200 |
| `src/interview/loop.ts` | Interactive walkthrough: prompt/persist answers, outcome accounting | `InterviewStore`, `InterviewIO`, `InterviewOutcome`, `InterviewRunOptions`, `runInterview` | ~220 |

Dependency direction after extraction:
`commands/interview.ts` → {section, qa, explanation, extraction, loop} →
{`../lib/llm.js`, `../lib/progress-feedback.js`, `../config.js`, `../types.js`} and
sibling modules only. `loop.ts` → `section.ts`, `qa.ts`, `extraction.ts`;
`extraction.ts` → `qa.ts`, `section.ts`. No module imports the entry barrel (AC4).

### Proposed child decomposition (structural slices)

1. **Foundation** — create `src/interview/` and extract `section.ts` + `qa.ts` (the pure,
   dependency-free parsing core). Blocks the rest.
2. **`explanation.ts`** — largest LLM cluster; independent of the loop.
3. **`extraction.ts`** — depends on `qa.ts`/`section.ts` for insert/merge helpers.
4. **`loop.ts`** — core walkthrough; depends on slices 1 and 3.
5. **Closeout** — thin the entry barrel (`src/commands/interview.ts`), lockstep split of
   `tests/cli/interview.test.ts`, module-map documentation, `wc -l` evidence, build +
   full suite.

Slices are ordered so slice 1 blocks the rest and each slice is independently move-only and
verifiable with the changed-scope test gate.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/interview.ts` — becomes entry + barrel; loses ~1,200 lines, keeps `register`
- `src/interview/section.ts` — new (heading detection/extraction)
- `src/interview/qa.ts` — new (parse/rebuild)
- `src/interview/explanation.ts` — new (producer-review explanation)
- `src/interview/extraction.ts` — new (LLM extraction + section insert/merge)
- `src/interview/loop.ts` — new (interactive walkthrough)
- `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` — split in lockstep into `tests/cli/interview/*.test.ts`
  (parsing/rebuild, loop + extraction, command integration, command `--llm`/progress,
  explanation), assertions verbatim
- `src/command-registry.ts` — read-only (specifier must keep resolving)
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — command/module map note for the new `src/interview/` modules
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `docs/design/incremental-sync.md`, `CLI.md` — read-only
  unless wording names the module layout (it does not today; verify, do not churn)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Silent behaviour drift in the re-serialiser** (the lossless round-trip is the command's
  subtle core; regexes are shared between parsing and rebuild). *Mitigation:* extract
  `qa.ts` first with zero edits, keep the 19 existing `describe` groups untouched, and land
  each slice as a separate move-only commit so a regression is bisectable.
- **Barrel/ESM resolution break.** `src/commands/interview.ts` must keep existing so
  `dist/commands/interview.js` is emitted; a `interview/index.ts` barrel would silently
  break the lazy registry. *Mitigation:* AC2 + the `lazy-command-registry` and
  `entry-point-split` suites as the oracle.
- **Circular imports** if `loop.ts` or `extraction.ts` reach back into the entry for types
  or helpers. *Mitigation:* AC4 — modules import siblings and `../lib/*` only; shared types
  live with their owning module (`section.ts`, `qa.ts`, `loop.ts`).
- **Test-file split churn.** 19 `describe` groups currently share one module scope.
  *Mitigation:* move groups verbatim; add no shared helper unless two target files need the
  same fixture, and then only a mechanical extraction.
- **Regrowth repeats.** This sweep already has a "completed" decomposition that never
  landed (see Related work). *Mitigation within scope:* documented single-responsibility
  module headers; the repo-wide guard is WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL (separate, low priority).
- **Scope creep risk.** The split invites opportunistic "while we're here" cleanups — a
  parser rewrite, prompt-tuning, a new `--flag`, splitting the 266-line `register` action
  into sub-commands. *Mitigation:* AC3 forbids logic edits; any such opportunity is filed
  as a separate item linked `discovered-from:WL-0MVGKGXN80006V9P` rather than absorbed.
- **Review fatigue on a wide-but-shallow diff.** A move-only refactor touches many files
  for zero behavioural gain, which can invite under-review. *Mitigation:* one concern per
  commit/slice, `git diff --color-moved` for reviewers, and the unchanged suites as the
  behaviour oracle.
- **Assumption:** the 1,000-line ceiling applies to non-test source, and to a test file only
  when it is touched in lockstep with its module (sweep rule; identical to
  WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT AC3).
- **Assumption:** the full 41-symbol public surface is retained in the barrel rather than
  trimmed to the 12 symbols tests import. Trimming would be a breaking change for any
  external plugin consumer and buys nothing here; the barrel re-export is ~10 lines.
- **Assumption:** no consumer call-site changes are acceptable — `src/command-registry.ts`
  and the CLI help output must be byte-identical for `wl interview`.
- **Assumption:** no behavioural improvement is bundled; opportunities observed en route
  become separate `discovered-from` items.

## Related work

- WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 — parent sweep/directive: every production file > 1,000 lines is
  evaluated for decomposition (producer Q1 answered).
- WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT — sibling from the same sweep (`packages/shared/src/database.ts`);
  source of the lockstep test-split rule reused in AC3 and the module-map layout pattern
  (entry façade + cohesive modules + explicit dependency direction).
- WL-0MULI1N1N0001WRD — "CLI: Explanation path & new options" (completed); introduced the
  `--no-llm`/`--json` modes and the producer-review explanation path extracted here. (The
  seed description labelled this item "Interview LLM fallback"; the title above is the
  accurate one — the LLM *extraction* fallback is WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF.)
- WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67 ("Interview replay feature"), WL-0MUUAMP7M008Z4GK ("r-i interview
  explanation does not state why an item needs producer review"), WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF
  ("interview: LLM-assisted question extraction as fallback"), WL-0MUX2W8IN005RW66
  ("Feedback in interview when running LLM"), WL-0MUQ0VP800068DNX ("Interview LLM config
  schema") — all completed; provenance items for the behaviour implemented in this file,
  cited in its doc comments and moving with their code.
- WL-0MUQ0VQ8A002HHFA — "Interview LLM fallback integration" (completed); the integration
  work behind the extraction fallback path extracted here.
- WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL — proposed repo-wide file-size guard (`discovered-from` the sweep);
  the reason this item's ceiling check is manual plus a small structural assertion.
- WL-0MVGKH6Z1000XWGJ, WL-0MVGKH9Z900178UF, WL-0MVGKH47T007GKN1, WL-0MVGKHCP9005SJPZ,
  WL-0MVGKHFT4003X6JW — companion god-class items from the same sweep (`init.ts`,
  `github-sync.ts`, `fetcher.ts`, `dispatcher-anchor.ts`, `downtime-log.ts`).
- Repo precedent for layout: `src/doctor/*` helper modules consumed by
  `src/commands/doctor.ts`.

## Appendix: decision log (agent-proposed; producer may override)

No producer interview questions were required: the seed context (goal, drafted ACs, parent
directive) plus two completed sibling intakes from the same sweep answer every open choice,
and all decisions below are reversible at plan/implement time. Recorded for review.

- **Q: Where should the extracted modules live?**
  **Recommended and chosen: `src/interview/`, mirroring the existing `src/doctor/`
  precedent** (top-level feature directory consumed by one command module). The entry stays
  `src/commands/interview.ts` so the ESM specifier `./commands/interview.js` keeps
  resolving under NodeNext.
  Alternatives considered: (b) flat siblings `src/commands/interview-*.ts` (works, but mixes
  six command-specific helpers into the already crowded flat `src/commands/` namespace);
  (c) a `src/commands/interview/index.ts` barrel (breaks the emitted
  `dist/commands/interview.js` specifier the lazy registry depends on).

- **Q: How granular should the split be?**
  **Recommended and chosen:** five extracted modules plus the entry (map above), one per
  existing section banner, each 95–400 lines — comfortably under the ceiling without
  inventing new boundaries mid-move.
  Alternatives considered: a two-way split (parsing vs everything else ≈ 470 / 1,150 lines —
  fails AC1); eight-plus micro-modules (churn without benefit).

- **Q: Keep the full 41-symbol barrel, or trim to the 12 symbols tests import?**
  **Recommended and chosen: keep the full surface.** The parent epic's "used symbols only"
  barrel decision (WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 Q2) applied to a module where unused symbols were
  genuinely internal; here every symbol is a documented part of this command module's
  surface and trimming risks breaking out-of-repo plugin imports for ~10 lines of saved
  barrel. Behaviour-parity is the priority (AC2).

- **Q: Split the oversized test suite in this item?**
  **Recommended and chosen: yes, mechanical lockstep split only.** `tests/cli/interview.test.ts`
  (1,696 lines) exceeds the same ceiling, and the parent sweep rule evaluates test files in
  lockstep with their module (identical to WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT AC3). Assertions, fixtures and
  `describe` titles are unchanged; only file location and import paths move.

- **Q: Add a file-size regression guard here?**
  **Recommended and chosen: no — out of scope.** A guard is repo-wide policy
  (WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL) affecting every sibling god-class item. This item records `wc -l`
  evidence and (optionally, if cheap) a structural assertion that the interview module
  family stays ≤ 1,000 lines; the repo-wide gate stays a separate item.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQDR51JO0037ISJ** – Eliminate unsafe as any casts in shortcut dispatch (detail view and duck-typing) (completed)
- **WL-0MQDR5ICN0098ID6** – Remove unused WorkItem import from index.ts (completed)

# Decompose the `src/commands/doctor.ts` god class

**File:** `src/commands/doctor.ts` (1,658 lines at intake time; 1,582 when the item was created)

## Problem statement

`src/commands/doctor.ts` is a single 1,658-line module that carries the entire
`wl doctor` CLI surface: six module-level notice/formatting helpers at the top
and eleven command registrations (root `doctor` validation, `upgrade`,
`stage-sync`, `prune`, `cache`, `foreign-items`, `audit-gaps`,
`dangling-parents`, `priority`, `file-paths`, `migrate`), each with its own
inline `async` action body. The `--fix` interactive flow and the findings
aggregation of the root command alone occupy ~385 lines inside one nested
callback. Navigating, reviewing or changing one subcommand requires holding the
other ten in view, so every doctor change carries avoidable regression risk and
the file sits above the 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted for
WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7.

## Users

- **CLI maintainers (agents and humans)** need to change one doctor subcommand
  (e.g. `prune`, `file-paths`, the `--fix` prompt) without reasoning about
  1,600 unrelated lines.
- **Reviewers/auditors** need a diff attributable to a single subcommand so the
  blast radius of a change is legible.
- **Future agents implementing doctor work items** (e.g. the open
  WL-0MVM8V79C003XH2J `wl doctor prefix` item) need a named, findable module
  per subcommand instead of appending to a monolith.

Example user stories:

- As an agent adding a new doctor subcommand, I want an existing per-subcommand
  module template so that registration is mechanical and reviewable.
- As a reviewer, I want a `prune` change to touch only the prune module and its
  tests so that I can verify it against its own suite.
- As a maintainer, I want every doctor file under 1,000 lines so that it is
  readable in a single pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports ≤1,000 for
   `src/commands/doctor.ts` (now a thin registrar) and for every module created
   by the split.
2. **Public entry point unchanged.** `src/commands/doctor.ts` still provides
   `export default function register(ctx: PluginContext): void`, so
   `src/command-registry.ts` (`doctor: () => import('./commands/doctor.js')`)
   and every existing CLI test import path keep working with **no importer
   edits**.
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No change to subcommand names,
   flags, help text, human output strings, JSON payload shapes or exit codes; no
   existing test file is modified (import paths, fixtures or assertions), and
   all existing `doctor` CLI/integration tests (`tests/cli/doctor-*.test.ts`,
   `tests/doctor-*.test.ts`) pass unmodified.
4. **One concern per module.** Each extracted module registers exactly one
   doctor subcommand — or, for the shared notices module, one cohesive
   cross-cutting concern — carries a module-level doc comment stating its single
   responsibility, and moves its provenance comments (work-item ids) with the
   code.
5. **No cycles, narrow seams.** Extracted modules never import from
   `src/commands/doctor.ts`; the registrar passes a narrow typed context
   (`program`/`output`/`utils` and `dataPath` only where needed) so handlers do
   not depend on the full `PluginContext` surface.
6. **Line-count guard test (additive).** A new test asserts the doctor module
   family stays at or under 1,000 lines per file and fails when any module
   exceeds the ceiling (mirrors the `downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts`
   precedent from WL-0MVLIHWOY003IP5E — no existing test is touched).
7. **Documentation updated.** Any repository notes that describe the doctor
   command layout (e.g. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CLI.md`, `docs/migrations.md`
   references) remain accurate, and the new module layout is stated in the
   top-of-file doc comment of `src/commands/doctor.ts`.
8. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate the existing action bodies and helpers into sibling
  modules, adjust imports and registration wiring; do not refactor their logic,
  rename flags, or reword user-facing output.
- **Entry point is fixed.** `src/commands/doctor.ts` must remain the dynamic
  import target in `src/command-registry.ts`; the split happens *behind* that
  path.
- **CLI-agnostic logic stays put.** `src/doctor/*.ts` holds CLI-independent
  validation logic (`status-stage-check`, `dependency-check`, `file-paths-check`,
  `hook-upgrade`, `foreign-items-check`, `audit-gaps-check`, `parent-check`,
  `podcast-scripts-check`, `fix`). It is consumed as-is; this item does not
  restructure it.
- **Serial, tree-green landing.** Extract the smallest subcommands first and the
  root validation/`--fix` action last, so every intermediate state builds and
  passes the suite.
- **No new runtime dependencies.** No changes to the doctor CLI contract, and no
  edits to the TUI or other commands.

## Existing state

`src/commands/doctor.ts` is 1,658 lines on today's `dev`. Inventory of logical
sections (line ranges from the current checkout):

| # | Section | Lines | Size |
|---|---------|-------|------|
| 1 | File header + imports | 1–30 | 30 |
| 2 | `DAY_MS` constant | 31 | 1 |
| 3 | `formatCacheBytes` helper | 33–46 | 14 |
| 4 | `DoctorOptions` type | 47–50 | 4 |
| 5 | `PendingUpgradeState` + `detectPendingUpgrades` | 51–92 | 42 |
| 6 | `buildPendingUpgradeFinding` | 93–129 | 37 |
| 7 | `printPendingUpgradeNotice` | 130–151 | 22 |
| 8 | `PendingCacheState` + `detectPendingCacheState` | 152–196 | 45 |
| 9 | `printPendingCacheNotice` | 197–207 | 11 |
| 10 | `register()` prologue + root `doctor` command definition | 208–217 | 10 |
| 11 | `doctor upgrade` action | 218–418 | 201 |
| 12 | `doctor stage-sync` action | 420–549 | 130 |
| 13 | `doctor prune` action | 551–649 | 99 |
| 14 | `doctor cache` action | 651–715 | 65 |
| 15 | `doctor foreign-items` action | 717–838 | 122 |
| 16 | `doctor audit-gaps` action | 840–877 | 38 |
| 17 | `doctor dangling-parents` action | 879–948 | 70 |
| 18 | `doctor priority` action | 950–1036 | 87 |
| 19 | `doctor file-paths` action | 1038–1150 | 113 |
| 20 | `doctor migrate` action | 1152–1271 | 120 |
| 21 | Root `doctor` action (findings aggregation, `--fix` interactive prompt, notices) | 1273–1657 | 385 |

Relevant structural facts discovered during intake:

- **Single consumer.** Only `src/command-registry.ts` imports the module
  (`doctor: () => import('./commands/doctor.js')`), and only for the default
  export. There is no cross-module use of helpers defined in the file, so
  extraction needs no public barrel beyond the unchanged default export.
- **Existing precedent for a nested sibling directory.** `src/sync.ts` (1,828
  lines, itself the subject of WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ) already sits beside a
  `src/sync/` directory (`src/sync/merge-utils.ts`), so `src/commands/doctor.ts`
  + `src/commands/doctor/` follows an established repository shape.
- **CLI layer vs validation layer.** `src/doctor/` modules are pure,
  `PluginContext`-free validators; the monolith's bulk is CLI registration and
  output rendering. The split therefore belongs in the command layer, not in
  `src/doctor/`.
- **Test surface to keep green (unmodified).** 18 existing doctor suites —
  `tests/doctor-{dependency-check,file-paths,foreign-items-apply,foreign-items-check,hook-upgrade,podcast-scripts,retired-stage,status-stage}.test.ts`
  and `tests/cli/doctor-{audit-gaps,cache,foreign-items-apply,foreign-items-push,foreign-items,priority,prune,stage-sync,upgrade-notice,upgrade}.test.ts`.
  Source: `ls tests/doctor-*.test.ts tests/cli/doctor-*.test.ts`.

## Desired change

Reduce `src/commands/doctor.ts` to a thin registrar that wires the root
`doctor` command and delegates each subcommand to its own module under a new
`src/commands/doctor/` directory. Starting decomposition (boundaries are an
implementation decision, subject to the constraints above):

| New module | Responsibility | Approx. size |

# Remove dead top-level `singleFork` key in vitest.config.ts

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 — Reduce time to run tests

## Problem statement

`vitest.config.ts` sets `singleFork: true` at the top level of the `test`
block. Vitest 4 has no such top-level option — `singleFork` is a
`poolOptions.forks.*` key — so the setting is silently ignored (no warning is
emitted). The comment directly above it, "Force per-file isolation by limiting
to 1 active worker per file sequence", describes behaviour that is actually
provided by `isolate: true` + `maxWorkers: 4` (+ `pool: 'forks'`).

The dead key is harmless today, but it is misleading: a future reader may
believe the suite is serialised, and a migration to an option shape that *is*
read (or vitest version churn that starts warning) could confuse diagnosis.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `singleFork: true` is removed from `vitest.config.ts`.
- The comment above it is rewritten (or removed) to state what actually
  enforces per-file isolation (`pool: 'forks'`, `isolate: true`,
  `maxWorkers: 4`), and that parallelism is otherwise intentional.
- Full canonical suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) stays green with the same
  test counts; no runtime regression in either wall-clock or aggregate test
  time on the same host.

## Out of scope

Bumping `maxWorkers` / `fileParallelism` — that is the follow-up "Test-suite
parallelism: reconsider maxWorkers on hosts with more cores".

## Summary

Discovered during a `/skill:machine-hygiene` session (approval-gate output).
`scripts/evaluate.py` renders the Proposed actions table more than once in the
same run, and the three `renice` actions (node, pi, npm-exec-tsx) are each
proposed as separate numbered actions (observed as 2-4 duplicated by 5-7).

Impact: the operator sees 8 actions where there are 5 distinct remediations,
polluting the approval gate. The duplicate rows are also indistinguishable, so
approving "1" while declining "5" leaves the same target both executed and
skipped.

Fix: dedupe keep-first on `(action, target pids | scope)` and render the gate
findings exactly once per run.

Source: `discovered-from:machine-hygiene-session-2025-10-21`.

## Verified root cause (plan session)

Reproduced against `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/` in the SorraAgents repo
(the installed copy at `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/` is byte-identical).

**A. Duplicate actions — `pressure_analysis.py`.**

- `analyze_pressures()` computes the top-3 RSS contributors **once**, then
  assigns the *same list object* to every elevated pressure
  (`pressure["contributors"] = contributors`).
- `propose_remediations()` loops pressures x contributors, emitting one
  `renice` per (pressure, contributor) for `memory_usage`, `memory_pressure`
  and `swap_usage`. Two elevated memory metrics x three contributors yields six
  `renice` actions for three distinct targets.
- `rank_actions()` only sorts by impact/risk ratio; it never dedupes, and
  `evaluate.py` never calls it.

Deterministic repro (synthetic metrics: `memory_usage` critical, `swap_usage`
warning, 3 RSS contributors): 6 actions, 3 distinct `(action, target)` pairs;
rows 1-3 are field-for-field identical to rows 4-6.

**B. Repeated rendering — `evaluate.py` / `tables.py`.**

- `render_approval_gate()` renders the Proposed actions table (copy 1).
- `prompt_for_approval()` renders it **again** before the prompt (copy 2).
- `render_human()` renders it a **third** time, together with a second copy of
  the before table and of the pressure analysis.

Measured on the interactive path: `## Proposed actions` appears 3 times and
`## Before` appears 2 times. On the `--yes` path the gate is skipped, so each
appears once. The work item's "twice" is therefore an undercount of the
interactive path, which is the observed run.

## Scope

In scope: dedupe proposals keep-first; render gate findings once per run.

Out of scope (recorded in Observations, not fixed here): `renice` safety checks
(current nice value, live test suites), ranking being unused by `evaluate.py`,
`--json` + interactive gating mixing prose and JSON, `TOP_CONTRIBUTORS` not
being configurable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `propose_remediations()` emits no two actions sharing a dedupe key
   of `(action, frozenset(target pids), target scope)`. A fixture with two
   elevated memory metrics (`memory_usage` + `swap_usage`) and three RSS
   contributors yields exactly 3 `renice` actions, not 6.
- **AC2** — Dedupe is keep-first: the surviving action is field-for-field
   identical to the first emitted duplicate (`action`, `target`, `reason`,
   `expected_impact`, `impact`, `risk`), so the relative order of distinct
   actions is unchanged.
- **AC3** — `rank_actions()` dedupes as well, so
   `rank_actions(propose_remediations(...))` and any caller passing a list that
   contains duplicates both return no duplicates ("dedupe before ranking").
- **AC4** — An interactive run prints the `## Proposed actions` table exactly
   once and the `## Before` table exactly once across the entire run (gate
   output plus final report), asserted with injected `input_fn`/`output_fn` and
   no real TTY.
- **AC5** — The `--yes` (auto-approve) path still prints both tables exactly
   once, and `--dry-run` and `--json` output shapes are unchanged.
- **AC6** — Approval stays row-accurate: approving row `n` of the displayed
   table approves that row, and `approved_count + declined_count` equals the
   number of displayed rows (no duplicate counted twice).

## Key Files

- `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/pressure_analysis.py` — add `dedupe_actions()`
  and apply it in `propose_remediations()` and `rank_actions()`.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/tables.py` — `prompt_for_approval()` gains
  `show_actions: bool = True` so a caller that already rendered the table can
  suppress the repeat; `render_approval_gate()` unchanged.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/evaluate.py` — record in the workflow result
  whether findings were already rendered; `render_human()` skips
  already-rendered findings; pass `show_actions=False` to the gate prompt.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_pressure_analysis.py` — dedupe unit tests.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_approval_gate.py` — single-render and
  row-accuracy tests.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_integration.py` — end-to-end section-count
  assertions for the interactive and `--yes` paths.

All paths are relative to the **SorraAgents** checkout
(`/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents`, branch `dev`). The installed copy under
`~/.pi/agent/skills/` is a build artefact refreshed by `scripts/install_pi.sh`
and must not be edited directly.

## Minimal implementation (test-first)

1. Add the failing tests first: duplicate-`renice` fixture (AC1/AC2),
   `rank_actions` dedupe (AC3), section counts for both paths (AC4/AC5),
   row accuracy (AC6).
2. `pressure_analysis.py`: `dedupe_actions(actions)` keyed on
   `(action, frozenset(pids | []), target.get("scope"))`, keeping the first
   occurrence; call it at the end of `propose_remediations()` and at the start
   of `rank_actions()`.
3. `tables.py`: add the `show_actions` parameter to `prompt_for_approval()`
   (default `True` preserves current behaviour and keeps existing tests green).
4. `evaluate.py`: add `findings_rendered` to the `run_workflow()` result (`True`
   when the gate printed findings); `render_human()` gains
   `include_findings: bool | None = None` defaulting to
   `not result.get("findings_rendered", False)`; pass `show_actions=False` in
   the gate's prompt call.
5. Docs: no `SKILL.md` change needed (internal behaviour); the skill tests are
   the contract.
6. Run the changed-scope test gate for the skill tests, then the dev-push full
   suite gate.

## Observations (not in scope — recorded, not fixed here)

- `renice` is proposed without inspecting the target's current nice value; the
  observed run targeted two live test suites already at nice 19/0. Tracked
  separately as a discovered item (see Appendix Q2).
- `evaluate.py` never calls `rank_actions()`, so actions are displayed in
  emission order rather than impact/risk order.
- `--json` without `--yes` still runs the interactive gate, mixing prose and
  JSON on stdout.
- `TOP_CONTRIBUTORS` is a module constant rather than a `config.yaml` tunable.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25 (plan): effort/risk pre-check returned `skip` (Extra Small / Low).
  Ran the six automated review stages against the existing content; rewrote the
  description with a verified root cause, six testable ACs, `Key Files` and a
  test-first implementation sketch. No children created (single vertical
  slice); AC coverage review returned `proceed`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Where does the fix land: the installed skill at
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/` or the SorraAgents repo?**
  Answer (plan, evidence-based): the SorraAgents repo,
  `skill/machine-hygiene/`, on branch `dev`. Evidence: `diff` shows all three
  scripts byte-identical between repo and installed copy, and prior
  machine-hygiene work shipped from `skill/machine-hygiene/`

## Summary

Add a `wl doctor prefix` subcommand that changes the configured project prefix in `.worklog/config.yaml` and renumbers every existing work item to the new prefix, preserving each item's suffix (e.g. `OSL-0MVK31VYQ007CN37` → `CC-0MVK31VYQ007CN37`). The flow must ask for confirmation before it changes anything, default to a read-only preview, and emit a machine-readable rename map.

## Motivation

Requested from the ContentCreator project (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator`), whose configured prefix is `OSL` while the project is now branded `CC`. 1207 work items carry the `OSL-` prefix, and `wl doctor foreign-items` correctly classifies any item whose prefix differs from `.worklog/config.yaml` as foreign — so editing the prefix by hand would make the whole backlog look foreign and break cross-project lookups.

## Scope (proposed)

- `wl doctor prefix` — read-only preview: current prefix, counts of items/comments/dependency edges/audit records, and sample renames.
- `wl doctor prefix --to <PREFIX>` — declare the target prefix (validated: non-empty, no `-`, ASCII alphanumeric).
- `wl doctor prefix --to <PREFIX> --confirm` — apply: rewrite the config prefix, then rewrite every ID-bearing record (`workitems.id`, parent references, dependency edges, comments' `workItemId`, audit results, waivers, and any other ID column), and write a rename map (`osl→cc` pairs) to `.worklog/prefix-rename-<timestamp>.json`.
- Confirmation gate: interactive run without `--confirm` prompts and requires an explicit `y`; a non-TTY run without `--confirm` aborts with no writes and a non-zero exit.
- Idempotent: re-running after a successful rename reports a no-op.
- `--json` output for scripting.
- Docs: `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` and `CLI.md`.

## Acceptance criteria (draft)

- [ ] `wl doctor prefix` (preview) reports counts and sample renames and changes nothing; covered by unit and temp-store integration tests.
- [ ] `--confirm` rewrites every ID-bearing record (items, parents, dependency edges, comments, audit results, waivers) and writes the rename map.
- [ ] Confirmation gate: non-interactive without `--confirm` aborts with a non-zero exit and zero writes; interactive requires explicit `y`.
- [ ] Re-running after a successful rename is a no-op, and a mid-run failure leaves the store recoverable (transactional or a documented rollback).
- [ ] `wl doctor foreign-items` reports zero foreign items after a confirmed rename.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated (CLI.md, DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md, code comments).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Out of scope

Rewriting ID references held outside the worklog store — code comments, docs, test fixtures, git commit messages, branch and worktree names. The requesting project owns that sweep and will use the rename map.

## Related

- Requested by work in the ContentCreator project (`discovered-from` recorded there).

# If Critical item is a child it should not show in top level herdr selection list (WL-0MVN4WESM007T4XI)

## Problem statement

The Herdr worklist renders critical-priority work items that have a `parentId` at the **top level** of the selection list, even when their parent is also listed — so a critical child appears twice: once as a standalone top-level row and once under its parent when expanded. The top level should contain only root items; a critical child must appear only as a child.

Confirmed live reproduction: `WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY` (critical, blocked, `intake_complete`, parent `WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0`) is a child of `WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0` (critical, in-progress). Both render at top level.

## Users

- **Producer / operator using the Herdr worklist** — browses the top-level selection list to choose what to work on next.
  - *As a producer, I want the top-level list to contain only root work items, so I am not shown the same unit of work twice and the list stays short enough to scan.*
- **Developer/agent triaging critical work** — needs release-blocking critical work to remain discoverable.
  - *As a triager, I want a critical child to be reachable from the top level via its parent, so hiding the duplicate row does not make the work invisible.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Top-level invariant**: the default Herdr worklist contains **no** item with a non-empty `parentId`, critical items included. Enforced on the merged set (browse feed + all mandatory subsets) for **both** fetch paths — the consolidated `wl worklist` bundle path (`assembleDefaultWorklist`) and the per-subset fallback — and by removing the `|| i.priority === 'critical'` exception from the root filter in `selectWorkItems`.
2. **Parent substitution preserves reachability**: when a critical child is dropped from the top level, its **root ancestor** (walking the `parentId` chain to the top-most non-child item) is included instead whenever that root is not already in the selected set. The substituted root joins the mandatory set (always shown, not subject to `browseItemCount`) and is sorted by its own priority/group. No badge, marker, or indicator is added to the substituted row.
3. **No regression for existing behaviour**:
   - non-critical children remain hidden from the top level exactly as today;
   - drill-down/expand still returns children unchanged (`fetchChildrenForItem` / `fetchChildrenForItems`, including critical children);
   - stage-filtered and priority-filtered views remain strictly root-only filters with **no** synthetic/substituted rows;
   - the CLI is unchanged for other consumers: `wl list --priority critical` still returns children (the ship critical-items gate must keep seeing them) and `wl worklist`'s `critical` subset keeps its current all-parent-levels query.
4. **Testing & validation**: unit tests cover the removed critical exception, the substitution rule (root ancestor promotion, parent already visible → no duplicate, parent in a non-critical group, count/mandatory interaction), and both fetch paths; the previously added critical-exception tests are updated/inverted. The full project test suite passes with the new changes.
5. **Documentation**: all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. At minimum: the root-filter comment in `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`, the critical-subset note in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` and `src/commands/worklist.ts`, and the Herdr worklist section of `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Constraints

- **No new hot-path `wl` spawn.** Root-ancestor resolution must use the existing in-process SQLite fast path first (`withInProcessDb` / refresh scope `db.get`), with `wl show` only as a fail-open fallback. The refresh-spawn budget work (WL-0MVI0IT4S0070G78, WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG) must not regress.
- **No data mutation.** Substitution is display-layer only: never rewrite the parent's stored `priority`, `status`, or `stage`.
- **Keep the `wl worklist` critical subset query as-is** (all parent levels, one spawn). It doubles as the discovery feed that tells the Herdr layer which parents to surface; making it root-only would require a second query per refresh.
- **Ship-gate semantics untouched.** `wl list --priority critical --status open` (exit code 7 gate) and the downtime critical candidate path keep their current child-inclusive behaviour.
- Fail-open: if a parent cannot be resolved (missing/deleted), the child is simply not shown at top level — never crash the refresh, never fall back to rendering the child at top level.

## Existing state

- **Why the duplicate exists today.** Commit `cae8ea8a` ("fix: show child critical items in worklist selection list") deliberately reintroduced critical children into the top level: the critical subset query dropped `--root-only` and `selectWorkItems` gained the `|| i.priority === 'critical'` root-filter exception. Rationale: child criticals (e.g. untriaged `[test-failure]` items) were invisible in the worklist while the ship critical-items gate still blocked release on them (exit code 7).
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — `selectWorkItems` root filter: `items.filter((i) => !i.parentId || i.priority === 'critical')`; `isMandatoryItem` treats any critical item as mandatory.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — `WORKLIST_LIST_SUBSET_QUERIES.critical = { priority: 'critical', status: ['open','in-progress','blocked','completed'] }` with **no** `rootOnly`, documented as "all parent levels: a critical child is as urgent as a critical root". `reviewQueue`, `inProgressRoots`, `blockedRoots` are all `rootOnly: true`.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchMandatorySubsets` issues `wl list --priority critical --status open,in-progress,blocked,completed` (no `--root-only`); `assembleDefaultWorklist` merges bundle subsets with the browse feed then calls `selectWorkItems` + `regroupWorkItems`; the per-subset fallback mirrors this. `fetchItemsByStage` / `fetchItemsByPriority` already pass `--root-only`.
- `wl worklist` is consumed only by `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (verified by search), so its payload shape is effectively a Herdr-internal contract.
- Current data: 174 critical items, 78 of them children — 77 of those are themselves `completed`/`done` (already filtered by the `stage !== 'done'` rule in `selectWorkItems`), leaving **one** live duplicate: `WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY`.
- The Pi TUI Worklog extension has no critical-subset or smart-selection code (removed by WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N), so no Pi-side change is needed.
- Parent rows already carry `childCount` (rendered as a `Children: N` metadata row and an expand icon), so a substituted parent is discoverable as a container.

## Desired change

1. **`packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`** — root filter becomes `items.filter((i) => !i.parentId)` (no critical exception). Update the doc comment to state the invariant and the substitution contract.
2. **`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`** — add a display-layer substitution step shared by `assembleDefaultWorklist` and the per-subset fallback:
   - partition the critical subset into root criticals (kept) and critical children (dropped from the top level);
   - for each critical child, resolve its root ancestor by walking `parentId` upward;
   - for each resolved root not already present in the merged candidate set, add it to the **mandatory** set (so `browseItemCount` cannot cut it) before `selectWorkItems` runs;
   - resolve parents in-process first (`db.get` via the refresh scope / `withInProcessDb`), falling back to `wl show`; unresolvable parents are skipped (fail-open).
3. **`src/commands/worklist.ts`** — documentation-only update: state that the `critical` subset is intentionally all-parent-levels (discovery feed) and that the top-level-only invariant is enforced by the Herdr consumer.
4. **Tests** — invert/extend `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.test.ts` (child critical hidden; non-critical children still hidden) and add fetcher-level coverage for both paths in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` plus the per-subset fallback tests.
5. **Docs** — update `packages/herdr/README.md` (worklist/selection behaviour) and the affected code comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — remove the critical exception from the root filter; document the invariant and substitution contract.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `assembleDefaultWorklist` + per-subset fallback: critical-child partition, root-ancestor resolution, mandatory-set injection; in-process-first parent lookup with `wl show` fail-open fallback.
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.test.ts` — invert the "shows child critical items at the top level" case; keep/extend non-critical child cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` — bundle path: child critical not rendered at top level; parent substituted and mandatory.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.test.ts` (per-subset fallback coverage, whichever file currently exercises `fetchNextItems` without the bundle) — same assertions on the fallback path.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — comment/documentation update for the `critical` subset (no behaviour change).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — selection-list behaviour documentation.

## Related work

- **WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR** — *Hide child work items from top-level selection lists (Pi and Herdr)* (completed). Introduced the root-only invariant; its critical-related behaviour was later superseded by commit `cae8ea8a`. This item restores the invariant for critical items while keeping reachability via parent substitution.
- **commit `cae8ea8a`** — "fix: show child critical items in worklist selection list" (no work-item reference in the commit message): the deliberate exception this item reverses. Its motivation — critical children flagged by the ship gate being invisible — is preserved through AC2.
- **WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1** — *wl next should return parent items instead of surfacing children individually* (completed): precedent for "represented by parent".
- **WL-0MQI1SX4W0018V9O** — *Child work items appear in Pi TUI selection list when they should be hidden (represented by parent)* (completed): same precedent, Pi side.
- **WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B** — *Selection list must always show all completed/in_review and critical items regardless of browseItemCount* (completed): defines the mandatory subsets whose "always shown" rule AC2 preserves for substituted parents.
- **WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C** — *Bubble up critical items* (completed): created the dedicated "Critical" group that sits first in the grouped output. Relevant because a substituted parent is **not** critical by priority, so it will not land in that group (see Risks).
- **WL-0MS7YCCLV000YJCR** — *Auto-downgrade critical children when parent priority is reduced* (completed): related priority-inheritance behaviour for critical children.
- **WL-0MV6KV22S004NYIU / WL-0MV71WBHB007D8ZE** — mandatory in-progress-root and blocked-root subsets: the sibling subsets that already use `--root-only`.
- **WL-0MVI0IT4S0070G78 / WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG** — spawn-budget work governing the consolidated `wl worklist` read and in-process refresh scope that the substitution must reuse.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Lost top-level visibility (accepted, mitigated).** Hiding critical children means an operator scanning only the top level no longer sees them directly; the ship critical-items gate can still block a release on a child. Mitigation: AC2 surfaces the root ancestor so the work stays reachable; the parent must be expanded to see the child itself.
- **Substituted parent is not marked critical** (operator decision Q3 = no indicator). It joins the mandatory set and is sorted by its own priority/group, so it may sit in a non-critical section. Risk: the release-blocking signal is less prominent. Accepted; revisit as a separate item if it proves insufficient.
- **Parent resolution cost.** Only critical children trigger a lookup, and only when the root is absent from the merged set (currently one such item). In-process read first; `wl show` is the rare fallback. A per-refresh memo should avoid repeat lookups within a tick.
- **Ancestor promotion depth.** A critical grandchild promotes its **top-most** ancestor, keeping the "no child at top level" invariant. Assumption: promoting the root (not the immediate parent) is correct because the top level may only contain roots.
- **Stage/priority-filtered views are exempt from substitution.** They are explicit filters ("every open item in this stage") and already root-only; injecting a synthetic parent row would misrepresent the filter. Accepted assumption: the ship-gate reachability requirement applies to the default worklist.
- **`wl worklist` payload keeps children in the `critical` subset.** Documented as the discovery feed; a future consumer reading the payload directly would still see children. Accepted, documented in `src/commands/worklist.ts`.
- **Scope creep.** No changes to grouping rules, detail views, badges, or the Pi TUI. Any follow-up (e.g. a critical-child indicator on parents) becomes a separate work item.
- **Assumption**: `parentId` is always present in the payloads used (`wl list`, `wl next`, `wl worklist`) — already relied upon by the existing root-only filters.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR** – Hide child work items from top-level selection lists (Pi and Herdr) (completed)
- **WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C** – Bubble up critical items (completed)
- **WL-0MQP4RDG2006LFM9** – Fix ruff lint findings in tests/test_audit_runner_core.py (completed) — *keyword-only match, unrelated*

### Repository file matches
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: another, appear, child, children, critical, extension, herdr, level, list, selection, should, show, they, top
- `CLI.md` — matched: same keywords
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: same keywords

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1** (intake round 1): "What should happen to a critical child whose parent is *not* otherwise in the top-level list (e.g. parent is `done`, or filtered out by the current stage/priority view)? (a) hide it entirely, (b) substitute the parent — show the parent row instead, (c) fallback exception — hide when the parent is visible, show the child when the parent is not, (d) freeform." — **Answer (user, interactive reply): "1. B"** — substitute the parent; the child is never rendered at top level.
- **Q2** (intake round 1): "Which lists should the fix cover? (a) default Herdr worklist only, (b) all Herdr top-level lists — default worklist, stage-filtered, priority-filtered, plus both fetch paths, (c) (b) plus CLI semantics, (d) freeform." — **Answer (user, interactive reply): "2. B"** — all Herdr top-level lists and both fetch paths; CLI `wl list`/ship-gate semantics unchanged.
- **Q3** (intake round 1): "Should a parent row show a 'critical child' indicator (badge/count) when it is surfaced because of a critical child?" — **Answer (user, interactive reply): "3. no"** — no indicator.
- **Derived assumptions (no question asked)**: (i) a critical child promotes its **top-most** ancestor, because the top level may only contain roots; (ii) stage/priority-filtered views get no substitution — they are explicit filters and already root-only; (iii) the substituted parent keeps its own priority/group (no critical marking, per Q3); (iv) an unresolvable parent means the child is simply not shown (fail-open).
- **Research note**: verified via `wl worklist --json` that the `critical` subset is the only mandatory subset without `rootOnly` (174 items, 78 children; 77 of those are `completed`/`done` and already filtered by the `stage !== 'done'` rule, leaving one live duplicate `WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY` under `WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0`). Traced the deliberate exception to commit `cae8ea8a` (no work-item reference) which removed `--root-only` from the critical query and added the `priority === 'critical'` root-filter exception to keep ship-gate-flagged child criticals visible. Confirmed `wl worklist` has a single consumer (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) and that `fetchItemsByStage`/`fetchItemsByPriority` already pass `--root-only`. Confirmed the Pi TUI has no critical-subset/smart-selection code.

Goal: a local-only pane whose prompt exceeds the local provider's context ceiling should degrade predictably instead of stalling or failing, and the reason should be visible to the operator.

Observed problem: the local provider rejects a local-only request when the projected prompt exceeds ~38k tokens warm, or ~25k on a cold prefix. Because the pane is labelled local-only the proxy refuses the local route, and the work is not processed on the local slot. Evidence in this deployment's route logs (.worklog/local-route.log, 697 turns across 5 roots): 49 turns route remote with fallbackReason resident_prefix_insufficient and 44 with large_context_bypass; 72 turns actually served local. The thresholds and the exact refusal behaviour (hard error vs silent fallback) live in the external llama-proxy (LP project), not in this repo - confirm before designing the fix.

Open design questions to settle in plan:
- Is the correct behaviour a fallback to remote for over-threshold requests, an explicit hard error surfaced to the operator, or pre-dispatch routing (choose remote-ok when the projected context exceeds the ceiling)?
- Where is the projected context size knowable? The pi extension sees the outgoing request (before_provider_headers), the dispatcher does not.
- Interaction with WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX (low priority -> local-only): over-threshold low-priority work must not become unprocessable.

# tree_coverage AC extraction silently ignores numbered acceptance-criteria lists

discovered-from:WL-0MVGB23MM004X501

## Problem

`skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` (`extract_acceptance_criteria`) only collects
markdown bullets that start with `- ` or `+ ` inside the `## Acceptance Criteria`
section. Work items whose ACs are a **numbered** list (`1. …`, `2. …`) yield an
empty AC set, so `run_coverage_review` reports `fully_covered: true` /
`recommendation: proceed` with **zero parent ACs** — the AC coverage gate passes
vacuously instead of verifying that children cover the parent.

Observed during planning of WL-0MVGB23MM004X501: `apply_coverage_review` returned
`action: proceed` with `parent_acs: 0` against a description containing nine
numbered ACs. Contributors have worked around it by manually normalising AC lists
to `- ` bullets (e.g. WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS, WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN) or by documenting
the limitation (WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7), which means the failure mode is invisible
unless an operator notices a 0-AC result.

## Desired outcome

1. `extract_acceptance_criteria` also parses numbered list items (`1. `, `1) `)
   inside the AC section, keeping continuation lines and inline code intact.
2. A parent section that has a `## Acceptance Criteria` heading but yields zero
   parsed ACs is reported as a **conflict/stop condition** (or an explicit
   warning in the review result) rather than silently `proceed`, so a silent
   vacuous pass is impossible.
3. Existing bullet-form ACs and all currently passing coverage reviews are
   unaffected (regression tests over both formats).
4. Documentation in the plan/intake skills notes the supported AC formats.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Numbered AC lists (`1. …`) and bullet lists (`- …`) are both extracted by
  `extract_acceptance_criteria`, with matching output for equivalent content.
- A numbered AC list in a work item description produces a non-zero
  `parent_acs` count from `run_coverage_review`.
- An `## Acceptance Criteria` section that parses to zero ACs no longer returns
  `recommendation: proceed` silently — it is surfaced as a conflict or explicit
  warning in the review result.
- Unit tests cover: numbered list, bullet list, mixed list, empty AC section, and
  the zero-AC stop/warn behaviour.
- Plan and intake skill docs state which AC formats the tooling recognises.

## Notes

- Workaround for items already affected: normalise the AC list to `- ` bullets
  (wording unchanged) so coverage can be computed.

# Audit fingerprint parity skew must never be silent (test + doctor)

Discovered-from: LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM (false-stale audit badge, 2026-10-25).

## Problem statement

`wl list` / `wl worklist` / review-queue grouping compute a *current* audit
content fingerprint with the TypeScript port (`src/audit-fingerprint.ts`,
**schema 2** since WL-0MVK5SWZE00254Y7 / commit `213a96b7`, 2026-10-23) and
compare it against the *stored* fingerprint persisted by the audit skill's
Python implementation (installed at `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts`,
sourced from SorraAgents `skill/audit`).

When the two sides compute **different payloads** (a `schema` key,
git-derived `path_states`, extra hash inputs), the digests can never match.
`isAuditFresh` (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts:457`) short-circuits on
`storedFingerprint === currentFingerprint` and returns false. Every audit
persisted under such a skew therefore renders as **out-of-date / stale** in
every `isAuditFresh`-driven view, even when the audit is genuinely current
and "Ready to close: Yes".

Observed on LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM: the stored fingerprint reproduced exactly
with the *then-installed* Python skill (pre-v2 formula
`{path_states, description_hash, key_files}`), yet `wl list` reported a
different `currentFingerprint` → the item showed as needing re-audit.

This skew is **silent** by design: `tests/unit/audit-fingerprint-parity.test.ts`
classifies any schema mismatch ("ahead or behind") as a **skip** that names the
installed schema — so the drift ships green and no-one is told that audit
freshness is broken end-to-end.

## Users

- **Worklog/agent operators** relying on audit freshness flags to know which
  `in_review` items truly need re-auditing; a false-stale flag wastes a
  re-audit and erodes trust in the queue.
- **Release-gate consumers** (`wl doctor audit-gaps`, review queue) that
  classify items via `isAuditFresh` / `assessAuditInvalidate`.

**User story:** "As a worklog operator, I want a fingerprint-schema skew
between the installed audit skill and this CLI to fail a test (or at minimum
surface as a `wl doctor` warning), so the false-stale audit badge cannot ship
silently."

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `evaluateInstalledContract` no longer treats a schema skew as a silent
  skip. A helper that declares a schema (any number) different from
  `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA` — ahead **or** behind — **fails** the
  parity test with an actionable message naming the installed schema, the
  expected schema, the scripts directory, and the remediation (port schema N
  in the installed skill, or point `AUDIT_SKILL_SCRIPTS` at one that does).
- AC2: a helper that declares **no schema** at all (pre-v2 install) is treated
  as skew: the test **fails** with a message naming the installed path and
  schema constant lookup, because an undeclared schema cannot be proven
  compatible (fail-safe: never claim parity on unprovable data). A test
  documents exactly the observed failure: a schema-1 Python report's stored
  fingerprint never matches the schema-2 `computeContentFingerprint` for the
  same title/description.
- AC3: genuine *environment unavailability* remains a skip, not a red herring:
  no scripts dir, no `python3`, or an unimportable helper each skip with the
  existing descriptive reason (CI images without the agent framework stay
  green).
- AC4: `wl doctor` gains a warning-level check
  (e.g. `audit-fingerprint.schema-skew`) that reports the installed vs
  expected schema and remediation when the installed audit skill's schema
  differs from `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA` or is undeclared. The check
  is a warning (non-failing) so existing workflows are not broken, but it
  appears in `wl doctor` output and `--json`.
- AC5: an end-to-end freshness test proves the reported failure mode and its
  fix: an item whose stored fingerprint was produced by a schema-2 Python
  report is `isAuditFresh`; a schema-1-report fingerprint (or a schema-1-style
  current computation) is not. The test is self-contained (in-memory
  audit-record fixtures) — this repo currently has **zero** fingerprint-bearing
  audits since the 2026-10-23 schema-2 port (verified: all 66 stored
  fingerprints predate it), so live data cannot be relied upon.
- AC6: docs updated: the module docstring in `src/audit-fingerprint.ts`, the
  parity test header, and `docs/dev/audit-fingerprint.md` state the new
  fail-on-skew contract (the old "skip on skew" rationale is removed — the
  table in `docs/dev/audit-fingerprint.md` § "Parity check and host tooling
  skew" still documents skip-on-skew and must be inverted).
- AC7: the full test suite passes with the changes. **No strictness env gate
  is required**: the schema-2 Python side has already shipped (SA-0MVIDI8E00063OOP
  `completed/done`; installed `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
  declares `_AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA = 2` at line 1222 and emits the
  schema-2 payload at line 2433, install 2026-10-26 00:50), so fail-on-skew is
  green on this host. Env-unavailability cases (AC3) remain skips.

## Constraints

- **No change to the fingerprint payload itself in this repo** — parity and
  diagnostics only.
- **Strict-by-default contract (operator-confirmed option 1A):** a host with a
  pre-v2 or undeclared-schema installed skill now *fails* the parity test and
  shows the `wl doctor` warning on purpose. This is the intended behaviour —
  the actionable message (AC1/AC2) tells the operator to reinstall the
  framework skills (`cd ~/projects/SorraAgents && git pull && scripts/install_pi.sh`)
  or point `AUDIT_SKILL_SCRIPTS` at a schema-2 install. A legacy
  `AUDIT_FINGERPRINT_PARITY_STRICT` env gate is **not** added (it would
  re-create the silence this item is meant to end).
- The skip path for missing environments (AC3) must be preserved; CI without
  `~/.pi/agent/skills` or `python3` must not fail.
- The `wl doctor` check (AC4) probes the installed skill the same way the
  parity test does (operator-confirmed option 2A): a `python3` subprocess
  reading `_AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA` and the helper signature, with a
  graceful skip when `python3`, the scripts dir, or the import is unavailable
  (mirrors AC3). One subprocess per `wl doctor` run is acceptable.

## Existing state (verified in repo)

- `src/audit-fingerprint.ts` — `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA = 2`;
  `computeContentFingerprint` hashes `{schema: 2, title_hash, description_hash}`
  with zero git calls (WL-0MVK5SWZE00254Y7).
- `tests/unit/audit-fingerprint-parity.test.ts` — `evaluateInstalledContract`
  returns a skip reason string for skew (`'installed audit skill at … implements
  schema <n> but this repository expects schema <expected>'`) and the unit test
  `'skips with the installed schema when the helper is ahead or behind'`
  (line ~146) asserts the skip. This is the line that must be inverted.
  `findAuditScripts()` / `pythonAvailable()` helpers already exist for the
  env-missing cases (AC3).
- Installed helper: `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` now
  declares `_AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA = 2` (line 1222) and computes
  the schema-2 payload via `_compute_content_fingerprint` (line ~2385-2433).
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts:444` `isAuditFresh` — primary gate is a bare
  string compare; mismatch ⇒ stale; no skew diagnostics (unchanged by this
  item — operator-confirmed option 3A keeps read paths untouched).
- Consumers seen today: `src/commands/grouping.ts:287`, `src/list-enrichment.ts`.
- `wl doctor` findings carry `checkId` / `severity: 'warning'` (e.g.
  `priority.invalid`, `upgrade.pending` in `src/commands/doctor.ts`) — the new
  check slots into that assembly; no doctor schema change needed.
- `docs/dev/audit-fingerprint.md` § "Parity check and host tooling skew" still
  documents the old skip-on-skew policy table (must be inverted per AC6).

## Desired change

1. **Invert the skew policy in the parity test.** `evaluateInstalledContract`
   (and its callers) now *fail* on any declared schema ≠ 2 and on an
   undeclared schema, with an actionable message. Environment-unavailability
   stays a skip (AC3). The two existing skew tests are updated from
   "skips" to "fails" and supplemented with an undeclared-schema case (AC2).
2. **Add a `wl doctor` warning check** `audit-fingerprint.schema-skew`
   (AC4) that probes the installed skill and reports installed vs expected
   schema + remediation in both human output and `--json`.
3. **Add a self-contained end-to-end freshness test** (AC5) proving a
   schema-2 stored fingerprint is fresh and a schema-1 one is not.
4. **Update documentation** (AC6) so the fail-on-skew contract is
   authoritative.

## Key Files

- `tests/unit/audit-fingerprint-parity.test.ts` — invert the skew policy;
  add undeclared-schema failure and the AC5 freshness test; keep AC3 skips.
- `src/audit-fingerprint.ts` — docstring update only (fail-on-skew contract);
  payload unchanged.
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — register the new warning check in the doctor
  findings assembly (human output + `--json`).
- `src/doctor/audit-fingerprint-skew-check.ts` (new) — installed-skill probe
  (shared shape with the parity test) + warning finding
  `audit-fingerprint.schema-skew`.
- `docs/dev/audit-fingerprint.md` — invert the skew-policy table and
  remediation text.
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — reference only; no behavioural change.

## Related work

- `WL-0MVK5SWZE00254Y7` (completed, bug) — schema-2 TS port; the skip-on-skew
  policy inverted here was introduced there.
- `WL-0MUEBQLRD00288VV` (completed, feature) — `audit_results` fingerprint
  column on existing DBs; underpins stored-vs-current comparison: with a NULL
  fingerprint the fallback time gate applies rather than a skew.
- `WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3` (completed, feature) — central read cache; relevant
  because the new `wl doctor` probe adds a subprocess to that path's tooling.
- `SA-0MVIDI8E00063OOP` (completed, SorraAgents, cross-repo) — the hard
  prerequisite; shipped and reinstalled (verified 2026-10-26).
- `LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM` — the observed false-stale audit that motivated this
  item; manual re-verification target after implementation.

See also the automated report appended in § "Related work (automated report)".

## Verification

- Unit: parity-test skew cases (ahead / behind / undeclared) fail with the
  actionable message; env-missing cases still skip; AC5 freshness test
  (schema-2 fresh, schema-1 stale).
- Integration: `wl doctor` on this repo's worklog shows no
  `audit-fingerprint.schema-skew` warning while the installed skill is schema
  2, and shows the warning + remediation when `AUDIT_SKILL_SCRIPTS` is pointed
  at a pre-v2 install (contract unit test).
- Manual: re-audit LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM after implementation and confirm
  `wl list` shows the audit fresh (stored == currentFingerprint).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Strictness of the parity test now the prerequisite (SA-0MVIDI8E00063OOP)
  has shipped?" — Answer (operator): "continue" — proceeded with the
  recommended option **1A: fail unconditionally on skew/undeclared schema;
  drop the `AUDIT_FINGERPRINT_PARITY_STRICT` gate**. Source: interactive
  reply "continue" to the intake round of 2026-10-27, where the recommendation
  was shown explicitly. Research: verified `audit_runner.py:1222` schema 2,
  SA-0MVIDI8E00063OOP `completed/done`.
- Q2: "How should the `wl doctor` check inspect the installed skill?" —
  Answer (operator): "continue" — proceeded with **2A: python3 subprocess
  probe mirroring the parity test; graceful skip on missing python3/scripts/
  import**. Source: interactive reply "continue".
- Q3: "Scope of skew surfacing beyond test + doctor?" — Answer (operator):
  "continue" — proceeded with **3A: parity test + `wl doctor` only;
  `isAuditFresh` / `wl list` unchanged**. Note: a `wl list` skew diagnostic
  (e.g. `fingerprintSkew: true`) was discussed and deliberately **out of
  scope** (recorded as a follow-up opportunity — see Risks). Source:
  interactive reply "continue".
- Research summary: the constraint in the original brief ("installed skill is
  still pre-v2; strict gate required") was found **stale** during intake — the
  installed skill now declares schema 2. This repo has zero fingerprint-bearing
  audits since 2026-10-23 (all 66 stored fingerprints predate the TS port), so
  AC5 must use in-memory fixtures rather than live data.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** a `wl list` skew diagnostic and richer `isAuditFresh`
  mismatch reporting are real opportunities but deliberately excluded (Q3).
  Track via a follow-up work item if the doctor warning proves insufficient.
- **Host-deployment surprise:** after this lands, any host still running a
  pre-v2 installed skill fails the parity test with an actionable message. This
  is the intended contract, but it is a new failure mode for the first run on
  a stale host — mitigated by the message clearly naming the remediation.
- **Assumption:** a single `python3` subprocess per `wl doctor` run is an
  acceptable cost. If doctor latency on this probe ever matters, it can be
  cached (cf. WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3).
- **Assumption:** `evaluateInstalledContract` stays a pure unit-testable
  function; the doctor check re-uses the same probe rather than duplicating
  import logic.
- **Failure mode:** if the installed skill later moves *ahead* of this repo

# Refactor guard: sync split invariants

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ — decompose `src/sync.ts` god class
**Type:** task (test-first gate — created and landed BEFORE any code moves)
**Position in chain:** 1 of 6 — blocks every extraction child.

## Goal

As a reviewer/auditor of the `src/sync.ts` split, I want one automated gate that
fails whenever the split breaks a behaviour-preserving invariant, so that every
extraction child can land safely, no existing test file changes, and no reviewer
has to re-derive the invariants by hand.

## Context

Parent AC2/AC3/AC4/AC1 require an unchanged public surface at `./sync.js`, an
unmodified test suite, an acyclic import graph, and no file above 1,000 lines.
Nothing in the root package enforces any of that today: there is no
`madge`/`dependency-cruiser`, the repo-wide file-size guard
(WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL) is still `idea`, and the only existing split guards are
the `packages/herdr` ones (`downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts`,
`index.split-guard.test.ts`) which are scoped to that package. This child
builds the enforcement first, mirroring the guard child of the sibling
decomposition (WL-0MVLIHWOY003IP5E for `downtime-worker.ts`) and the
`packages/shared` equivalent (WL-0MVOBOX1U0013HNF).

Facts captured at plan time (2026-10-26, `dev` @ `f39b2463`-era tree):

- `src/sync.ts` — 1,867 lines, **34 exports = 25 value exports (functions and
  one `const`) + 9 type exports (8 `interface` + 1 `type` alias)**. (The parent
  description's "23 functions/consts + 11 interfaces/types" split is corrected
  here; the total of 34 is unchanged.)
- 10 source files import from `./sync.js` / `../sync.js`: `src/database.ts`,
  `src/logging.ts`, `src/api.ts`, `src/index.ts`,
  `src/commands/{sync,init,migrate,helpers,doctor,delete}.ts`.
- 11 test files import from `../src/sync.js` (two of them via dynamic
  `await import()`): `sync.test.ts`, `sync-whitelist.test.ts`,
  `sync-author-gate.test.ts`, `sync-worktree.test.ts`,
  `rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts`, `sync-regression-guard.test.ts`,
  `sync-prefix-filter.test.ts`, `config-sync-allowed-authors.test.ts`,
  `sync-audit-results.test.ts`, `unit/audit-sync-monotonic.test.ts`,
  `cli/git-mock-roundtrip.test.ts`.
- 1 internal importer: `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` imports `type { MergeOptions }`
  from `'../sync.js'` — the only known would-be cycle, to be re-pointed at
  `src/sync/types.ts` by child 2.

## Acceptance Criteria


1. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** Every file in the resulting structure — `src/sync.ts` and every `src/sync*.ts` / `src/sync/**/*.ts` module — is ≤ 1,000 lines.
   Verified mechanically (`wc -l`) and recorded in the completion comment, driven
   by an exported `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` that initially contains only `'sync.ts'` and
   is asserted to only ever shrink (remain a subset of the plan-time list).
2. **Public API surface preserved.** All 34 existing exports remain importable from `'./sync.js'`.
   The committed baseline `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` records the 34
   symbol names (25 value + 9 type, flagged separately) plus provenance
   (generation command, source commit, timestamp), and a machine gate fails the
   suite when any one is lost — value exports resolvable at runtime, type
   exports present in the emitted declaration.
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only.** No logic changes; existing tests pass without modification.
   The guard's completion evidence shows zero diffs across the 77 existing test
   files; any accidental behavioural delta is reverted, not "fixed" in place.
4. **No new circular imports.** Dependency direction is acyclic and recorded in the module responsibility table.
   The static import graph of `src/sync.ts` + `src/sync/**/*.ts` contains no
   cycle (no module imports a module that imports it back); after the final child
   no production module under `src/sync/` contains a runtime (value) import of
   `'../sync.js'`. The gate is green now — the single `merge-utils.ts` type-only
   import sits in an explicit allowlist that child 2 removes — and red on any new
   violation.
5. **Module responsibilities documented.** Each extracted file carries a top-level JSDoc comment naming its concern.
   The guard suite itself is documented the same way, so the standard is
   established before the extraction children land.
6. New **additive** test file `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` (vitest) exists
   and passes on the current tree before any production code moves; no existing
   test file is modified.
7. **Negative proofs.** Each of the three gates is proven to fail on a
   deliberately broken input (synthetic >1,000-line module, dropped export,
   synthetic import cycle) — the failure modes are unit-tested, not assumed.
8. **Validation.** Full project test suite passes via the test skill, and `npm run build` — for this child, `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes including the
   new guard suite, and `npm run build` succeeds.

## Minimal implementation

1. Generate the baseline from `src/sync.ts` (regex-free, TypeScript compiler
   API or `tsc`-emitted `.d.ts` after `npm run build`) — normalise, sort,
   flag value-vs-type, and write JSON with provenance fields.
2. Write `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` with one named `it()` per gate
   (surface, size + allowlist, cycle/barrel, negative proofs) so failures are
   legible.
3. Put the pure predicates (parse module → imports/exports; build graph; find
   cycles) in `tests/sync/split-guard-scan.ts` so the negative-proof tests can
   feed them synthetic sources without touching the tree.
4. Export `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` and `TYPE_ONLY_BARREL_ALLOWLIST` so child 2 and
   child 6 can shrink them by one line each.
5. Record the baseline generation command in the file header, then run
   `/skill:test` (changed scope) and `npm run build` and paste both outcomes in
   a comment on this item.

## Key Files

- `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` — new guard suite.
- `tests/sync/split-guard-scan.ts` — new pure gate predicates/scanners.
- `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` — new frozen export baseline.
- `src/sync.ts` — read-only in this child (no edits).
- `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` — read-only in this child (allowlisted).

## Dependencies

None — first child. Every extraction child (2–6) is blocked by this one.

## Constraints

- Move-only / additive: production code and existing tests are untouched.
- Do not add `madge`, `dependency-cruiser` or any new runtime/dev dependency —
  graph and size checks are plain TypeScript.
- No edits to the `packages/herdr` split guards and no relocation of their
  `scan.ts`; this guard is root-package-scoped. Sharing a common scanner with
  the other packages is deliberately out of scope (would widen blast radius).
- A repo-wide file-size guard remains WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL; this guard covers
  only `sync.ts` and `sync/`.

## Deliverables

Frozen export baseline, guard suite + scanners, negative proofs, green
`/skill:test` (changed scope) and green `npm run build` recorded in a comment.
